keyFinding.interpretation: On the only reconstructable multi-name date, current PriorityScore-weighted capital concentrated conservative buyHigh projected stop risk more than equal-capital. This is a structural observation, not an outcome claim.

plans.note: Single-name date; all three allocation schemes are identical.

falsification.propositionRejected: PriorityScore-weighted allocation is mechanically risk-neutral with respect to planned stop geometry.
falsification.observedMechanism: On 2026-09-18, the highest PriorityScore name (3105) also had the widest conservative planned stop distance, so score-weighted capital and stop distance compounded into the largest projected risk contribution.
counterevidenceAndLimits: Only one reconstructable multi-name date exists; no predictive or OOS inference is allowed.
Equal-planned-stop-risk is an unconstrained diagnostic and would allocate 75029.23 NTD to 2006, 37.51% of total capital, above the current 35% per-name cap.
No return, MFE, MAE, stop-first, fill or realized drawdown data were used.
The observation does not prove equal-risk sizing improves returns or drawdowns.
A/B channel, volatility, regime, PriorityScore and transaction/execution constraints remain required controls.
